title: Look up a bank's reason code

blocks.text: When a bank rejects a transfer, it sends a four-character reason code such as `AM04`, and the payments team works from the `Reason` it stands for. The table of reasons is edited by hand whenever the bank publishes new codes, and the bank sometimes starts sending a code before the table has it.

items: `index(items, codeOf)`: the code-to-item index that `Reason` builds once from its constants;

blocks.text: When you're done, every code in the table finds its reason. A table in which two entries share a code is refused with an `IllegalArgumentException` naming the code, rather than quietly keeping one of them, and a code the table doesn't have yet comes back as unknown, so whoever handles the rejection can tell it from a code the bank explained. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: every code in the table finds its reason
the index holds each item of a table under its own code
a table with one code on two entries is refused, naming the code, instead of keeping the last entry
a code the table doesn't have comes back empty, not as a catch-all reason

origin.section: Look a Constant Up by Its Code Through a Map Built After the Constants, and Let It Refuse Duplicates

concepts: A code-to-constant index built from values() after the constants finds constants by a field, reports unknown codes as empty, and refuses duplicate codes instead of keeping the last.
